modules.title: Neovim Grammar: Verbs, Text Objects & Counts
modules.subtitle: Stop mashing arrows and Backspace—speak Vim's composable verb + object language.
modules.summary: Every Neovim edit is `<operator><motion/text-object>`: `ci"` changes inside quotes, `daw` deletes a word + trailing space, `dt,` deletes up to a comma.

sections.title: 1.1 Composable Editing (`operator` + `text-object`)
sections.body: Instead of moving to the start of a string and hitting `x` ten times, put your cursor anywhere inside quotes and press `ci"` (change inner quotes). Combine operators (`d`, `c`, `y`, `v`) with text objects (`iw`, `aw`, `i"`, `i(`, `i{`, `ip`) to multiply editing speed.
sections.code_example:
ci"   -> change inside double quotes
da(   -> delete around parentheses (including parens)
5j    -> jump down 5 relative lines
:%s/old/new/g -> substitute across entire buffer

modules.title: Macros & Repeat (`.`, `qa...q`, `@a`)
modules.subtitle: Automate repetitive multi-line edits in seconds with recorded macros.
modules.summary: Record an edit once into register `a` (`qa ... q`), replay with `@a`, and scale with `5@a` or visual `:normal @a`.

sections.title: 2.1 Recording Clean Macros
sections.body: Always start a macro with a canonical anchor like `0` or `^` (beginning of line) and end with `j` (next line) so replaying `10@a` never drifts off alignment!
sections.code_example:
qa        " start recording into register a
I"<Esc>   " insert opening quote at line start
A",<Esc>  " append closing quote + comma at line end
j         " move down to next line
q         " stop recording
3@a       " replay 3 times!

modules.title: FastAPI Routes, Pydantic v2 & TestClient
modules.subtitle: Build typed REST APIs with automatic OpenAPI docs and request validation.
modules.summary: Declare Pydantic request models, return proper HTTP status codes, and verify routes with FastAPI's `TestClient` right from Neovim.

sections.title: 1.1 Pydantic Validation & Status Codes
sections.body: FastAPI inspects Python type annotations and Pydantic `BaseModel` schemas to parse JSON bodies, validate constraints (`Field(min_length=1, ge=0)`), and automatically return `422 Unprocessable Entity` on bad payloads.

spec.question: What HTTP status code does FastAPI automatically return when a client sends a JSON body that violates a Pydantic `BaseModel` constraint?
spec.explanation: FastAPI returns `422` with structured error locations detailing exactly which field failed validation.
spec.hint: It is the RFC standard status code for semantic validation errors.

activities.title: Neovim Lab: Build a Typed Prompt Evaluation API

spec.instructions:
Build a FastAPI app in `api.py` exposing:
1. `GET /health` -> `{"status": "ok"}`
2. `POST /runs` (status `201`) accepting `RunCreate(model: str, score: float)` where `0.0 <= score <= 1.0`, storing runs in memory and returning `{"id": <1-based int>, "model": ..., "score": ...}`.
3. `GET /runs/{run_id}` -> returns the run or raises `404` if missing.
spec.test_code:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import api

def test_fastapi_endpoints():
    api.RUNS.clear()
    client = TestClient(api.app)
    r = client.get('/health')
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json() == {'status': 'ok'}

    bad = client.post('/runs', json={'model': 'qwen', 'score': 1.5})
    assert bad.status_code == 422

    created = client.post('/runs', json={'model': 'qwen', 'score': 0.92})
    assert created.status_code == 201
    body = created.json()
    assert body['id'] == 1 and body['model'] == 'qwen' and body['score'] == 0.92

    fetched = client.get('/runs/1')
    assert fetched.status_code == 200 and fetched.json()['score'] == 0.92

    missing = client.get('/runs/999')
    assert missing.status_code == 404
hints: Raise `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail='Not found')` when `run_id not in RUNS`.

modules.title: Defensive Bash Scripting & Text Pipelines
modules.subtitle: Write crash-safe shell tools with strict mode, quoting, grep, and awk.
modules.summary: Prevent silent shell bugs with `set -euo pipefail`, double-quote variables, and process log streams cleanly.

sections.title: 1.1 Unofficial Bash Strict Mode
sections.body: Starting scripts with `set -euo pipefail` stops immediately on any failing command (`-e`), errors on unset variables (`-u`), and ensures a failing command in the middle of a pipe isn't hidden (`-o pipefail`). Always double-quote `"$var"` to protect spaces!
sections.code_example:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
file="${1:?missing input file}"
grep -c 'ERROR' "$file" || true

spec.question: Without `set -o pipefail`, what exit code does `false | true` return in Bash?
spec.explanation: By default Bash only returns the exit status of the LAST command in a pipeline (`true` -> 0), silently swallowing failures earlier in the pipe!
spec.hint: Look at the rightmost command in `false | true`.

blanks.hint: exit on error + error on unset var

spec.explanation: `set -eu -o pipefail` (or `set -euo pipefail`) catches silent errors immediately.

activities.title: Neovim Lab: Log Error Counter Script

spec.instructions:
Write a Bash script `count_errors.sh` taking a log filename as `$1`.
- If `$1` is missing or the file does not exist, exit with code `1`.
- Otherwise print ONLY the integer count of lines containing `ERROR` (print `0` if none).

fixture_files.train.log:
INFO start
ERROR oom
INFO step 2
ERROR nan loss

hints: Remember `grep -c` exits with status 1 when count is 0! Use `grep -c 'ERROR' "$1" || true`.

modules.title: Git Internals: Branches, Commits & Clean Merges
modules.subtitle: Treat Git commits as an immutable DAG—branch, commit, and merge with confidence.
modules.summary: Understand HEAD and branch pointers, then complete a real sandbox Git branching quest graded directly on your repository history!

sections.title: 1.1 Branches Are Just Movable Pointers
sections.body: A Git branch is literally a 41-byte file holding a commit SHA. Creating a branch (`git switch -c feat/login`) is instantaneous because Git never copies files—it only moves pointers as you commit.
sections.code_example:
git switch -c feat/metrics
# edit files in Neovim
git add metrics.py
git commit -m "Add training metrics"
git switch main
git merge feat/metrics

activities.title: Participation Activity: What Is a Git Branch?

spec.question: Under the hood in `.git/refs/heads/`, what is a Git branch actually stored as?
options: A full zip copy of the repository
A lightweight pointer to a specific commit hash
A list of diff patches from commit 1
spec.explanation: Branches are lightweight pointers to commit objects; commits point to parent commits forming a DAG.
spec.hint: Why can Git create a branch in 1 millisecond even on huge repos?

activities.title: Real Git Sandbox Lab: Feature Branch & Merge

spec.instructions:
Inside this sandbox git repository:
1. Create and switch to branch `feat/neovim-docs`.
2. Edit `README.md` in Neovim to add the line `Status: ready` and commit it.
3. Switch back to `main` and merge `feat/neovim-docs` into `main` so working tree is clean.
4. Save or run `<leader>qt` (`devquest check`) to verify your Git graph!
hints: Run `git switch -c feat/neovim-docs`, edit README.md, `git add README.md && git commit -m 'Add status'`.
Then `git switch main && git merge feat/neovim-docs`.
